The Reaper Opinion Thread. Let's talk about our feelings (towards Reaper)!

Hey there, long time hobbyist user of Reason. I was using Reason up to version 6.5 up until recently, but always felt using it was awkward at best, and trying to conform to it's interface was slowing me down. So I checked out a lot of other DAWs, and have been using Reaper quite a bit for the last few months. I love editing in the sequencer, it's very intuitive and you can do so many functions with the mouse (unlike in Reason where you have to have your free hand poised over the QWERTY keys). And yes, the price is great (not free, $60 U.S. for a license). What I don't like about Reaper is its synthesizers, so I use Reason's synths via Rewire and that works like a champ. I also like that they are constantly updating for bug fixes and the like. Also, their user forum is quite active; lots of good info to be had there (unlike Reason which closed its forums and users are stuck using their facebook page)

I'm a professional producer / musician, and Reaper is my DAW of choice. I went from ProTools (pre-HD) to Logic and then I found Reaper. It's certainly not the most intuitive DAW out there, but moving from one to another is pretty difficult anyway. I have to use Studio One to interact with a few clients, and it's difficult to get a grasp on when I haven't used it for a while. There are things I would change, but they are minor. I trust Reaper to help me get my job done every day, and it hasn't let me down!

I have two: a 40" 4k30hz TV (attached to media centre pc, also my wife's favourite pc) and a 28" 4k60hz pc monitor, attached to my gaming pc.

For gaming, 4k is insanely awesome, but complicated. You need sli or crossfire if you want 60fps, and so that's what I do. But some games don't support it, and then they run like arse. I would pick 1440p but get 144hz instead for gaming today, except for how awesome having a 4k desktop is.

4k for general purpose computing and work (I'm a software developer) is awesome. If your eyesight is good you get more real estate, if it's bad you scale more and get super crisp images and text. Watch out for the odd application that doesn't support hidpi or retina, that's the only downside. Note that 30hz sucks balls, don't compromise on it. My wife doesn't seem to notice, but it's very uncomfortable for me.
